newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi sets up mining company to tap minerals.
newsitem.headline: Saudi sets up mining company to tap minerals.

text.p: Saudi Arabia is setting up a state-owned mining firm to search for minerals as part of efforts to diversify its oil-based economy.

Oil and Minerals Minister Ali bin Ibrahim al-Nuaimi told the official Saudi press agency SPA late on Wednesday the Saudi Arabian Mining Co, Maadin, would not have a monopoly over the lucrative mining sector and would operate on a commercial basis.
King Fahd last week issued a decree endorsing the creation of the long-awaited firm whose capital has not been disclosed.
Nuaimi said Maadin's administrative structure was being worked out and recruitments were being made.

He said Maadin, to be based in Riyadh, would be fully or partly offered for public subscription at a later stage, after its shows profit and its economic feasibility is proven "so as not to burden the shareholder or the government".

The world's richest oil producer already mines eight tonnes of gold a year, but its wealth of zinc, copper, bauxite, silver, phosphates, iron and more gold are awaiting to be exploited as part of a drive to reduce reliance on oil earnings of $40 billion yearly.

Analysts have said slow government approval for exploration licences is holding back development of the sector, which is forecast to grow faster than any other in the state's five-year plan to 2000, at an average annual rate of nine percent.
Nuaimi said Maadin would help provide more jobs for Saudis and seek to lure the private sector into mining, so far hampered by lack of infrastructure at remote mining sites and high costs.

"Its basic aim is to organise the mining sector, push it forward and unify mining projects which Saudi Arabia owns or participates in," he told SPA. "It will not have a concession over all mining areas in the kingdom.

"The relationship between Maadin and other private sector mining companies will be based on complementarity, not competition while laws applying to all companies that seek exploration licences will be applied to Maadin," he said.
Nuaimi said Maadin would "specialise in various mining projects, independently or through participation of the Saudi private sector or foreign companies".

He said it would initially run the Mahad adh-Dhahab gold mine and the Saudi Company for Precious Metals, which together with Swedish firm Boliden Mineral Aktiebolag, a unit of Trelleborg, runs the Sukhaybarat gold mine.
